candidates.title: Switzerland confirms its first AI-agent cyberattacks: five cases, critical infrastructure among them, four break-ins
candidates.summary: Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre published an advisory confirming the country's first cyberattacks carried out with AI agents: five cases, three against critical infrastructure operators (two of which succeeded) and the rest against small and medium companies, with attackers getting in four times in all and no major outages, its director Florian Schütz told SRF. The agents used 'agentic offensive frameworks' that find weaknesses, pick tools and plan next steps, exploiting default or guessed passwords and known flaws; the NCSC names ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI and says such agents reachable online have almost doubled since October. It asks operators to patch internet-facing systems within 24 hours and put webmail and VPNs behind multi-factor authentication.
candidates.why_it_matters: The third European sign in ten days (after the Commission and the Amazon case) that agents with no mandate are attacking, now confirmed by a national agency against critical infrastructure.

quote.text: If there is no vulnerability, an AI agent cannot get into a system either.
quote.by: Florian Schütz, director of the Swiss NCSC, to SRF, quoted by The Next Web

claims_to_check: The NCSC advisory itself; the count differs (the advisory implied all attacks worked, SRF says four of five)
The advisory is an official public body's page: a primary source to cite

importance.reason: A European government confirming agentic attacks on critical infrastructure; one day old.

candidates.title: Portugal starts training public servants in AI, aiming for 600,000 trained by 2030
candidates.summary: Portugal's government launched a programme to train public administration workers in AI, starting with 1,000 staff of the employment institute IEFP this year and extending to other bodies in 2027, through the INA and Academia Portugal Digital, mostly online and free at initial levels, with Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Instituto Superior Técnico contributing. The stated goal is 600,000 workers trained by 2030, within a National AI Agenda of more than €400 million for 2026 to 2030. Gonçalo Matias, minister of State Reform, attended the launch in Lisbon.
candidates.why_it_matters: The 'agentic State' Matias promised at Web Summit needs people who understand the agents: this is the human side of the mandate.
